label: SOFTWARE_STACK_REGISTRY: what is in use and how it is checked; not evidence and not authority
owner: STACK.md (narrative) + this file (machine-readable); code is the authority and both mirror it

adoption_levels.ADOPTED: in use, exercised by CI or the workflow, and its behaviour is verified in this repository
adoption_levels.STAGED: interface and acceptance criteria are written and executable, but the tool is not installed, not exercised, and produces nothing authoritative
adoption_levels.DEFERRED: deliberately not built; the contract is recorded so later work is implementation rather than redesign
adoption_levels.RESOLVED: decided by a measured rule: each candidate explicitly adopted or rejected, the decision committed and re-derived on a hosted runner; nothing is in force beyond what the decision says

invariants: additive: no scientific model imports an integration, and no integration's output is a model input
workspace-only: every writer refuses to write outside verification/ (scientific/workspace.py)
no authority effect: authority_effect = NONE for every element; none may admit or promote a result
fail-closed optionality: an absent optional dependency reports UNAVAILABLE and nothing is recorded as a pass
deterministic bytes: every governed artifact is reproducible byte-for-byte from the same inputs on the same backend

elements.name: Python scientific core (NumPy / SciPy)
elements.authority: scientific/models: each model's own numerics, identified by the digest of its source closure
elements.boundary: the arithmetic the scientific models run on; a model's result is admitted only through an independent check and a distinct reviewer, never because NumPy or SciPy computed it

elements.name: Snakemake workflow
elements.boundary: orders the governed workflow and writes only under verification/; it decides nothing -- the authority store does

elements.name: uv (resolution and environment)
elements.boundary: optional integrations are project extras, not dependency groups, so `uv sync --all-groups` stays lean

elements.name: Reproducible container
elements.boundary: the image fixes the software environment, not the host CPU: numerical bytes may differ between runners and are compared under the equivalence policy, never required equal. Built and run on a hosted runner on every push to the branch: digest-pinned base confirmed against the served manifest, non-root user, no host virtualenv, the harness's audits and the generic end-to-end demonstration run in the image and compared with the same demonstration run natively. It certifies the runs it hosts, never a scientific result.
elements.verification: bash container_verify.sh (inside the image); .github/workflows/container-verify.yml builds, runs and compares it on a hosted runner

elements.name: pytest + Hypothesis
elements.boundary: software verification only; a passing suite never converts a simulation into a measurement

elements.name: Ruff + mypy + Pydantic
elements.boundary: static discipline and trusted-boundary validation only; the Pydantic models validate hand-editable documents (this registry among them) and never become a competing vocabulary authority
elements.verification: python tools/typecheck_scope.py check  # and ruff over every tracked Python file; tests/test_typecheck_scope.py

elements.name: HDF5 data layer
elements.authority: scientific/hdf5_bundle.py: a ResultBundle written to HDF5 and read back exactly
elements.boundary: representation only; a bundle read back from HDF5 is checked against the one written, and is never evidence of admission

elements.name: RO-Crate packaging
elements.boundary: metadata packaging only; the crate restates what is not claimed and adds no evidence; the community validator runs beside the in-repo one on a hosted runner

elements.name: SLSA provenance + Sigstore signing
elements.boundary: a signature attests origin and integrity only, never scientific validity. What is adopted: the release candidate built deterministically for the commit (source archive, CycloneDX SBOM, SLSA-v1-layout provenance, index), signed with the workflow's GitHub OIDC identity, verified online and offline against the EXACT pinned identity and issuer, and a tamper suite run on a signed copy, on a hosted runner on every push to the branch. No SLSA build level is claimed: the provenance is produced by the workflow it describes, not by an isolated builder.
elements.verification: python tools/supply_chain.py verify --dir rc --mode online|offline|digests  # the hosted supply-chain job
open_items: no release is published and no tag is created: publication needs the owner's separate authorization
no SLSA build level is claimed

elements.name: Governed read-only retrieval over reviewed documents
elements.boundary: retrieval only -- verbatim cited spans, no generation, no network, no model client; retrieved text is never evidence, and only documents a reviewed commit allowlisted are read

elements.name: ParaView / VTK field export
elements.boundary: serializes a solved cell-centred field unchanged and reads it back at a stated tolerance; no resampling, no smoothing, not evidence

elements.name: OpenUSD scene export
elements.optional_dependency: usd-core (extra: viz) -- validation only; the .usda text is written directly
elements.boundary: geometric representation of a model's domain and its reported probes; no prim is a model input, and the stage is not evidence

elements.name: SALib global sensitivity cross-check
elements.authority: scientific/sensitivity.py: one-at-a-time and Sobol rankings of a model's response, compared at declared resolution
elements.boundary: a disagreement between the local and the global ranking is reported as METHODS_DISAGREE and REQUIRES_HUMAN_INTERPRETATION, never resolved automatically; NON_AUTHORITATIVE

elements.name: OpenMDAO design-space exploration
elements.boundary: explores only a model's declared, numeric, in-bounds parameters; every case is cross-checked byte for byte against a direct run; the report is EXPLORATION_ONLY NOT_A_RECOMMENDATION and not evidence

elements.name: FEniCSx (dolfinx) independent verifier
elements.authority: the governed producers in scientific/models remain the producers; FEniCSx is an INDEPENDENT_IMPLEMENTATION check whose verdict reaches authority only through the check contract and a distinct reviewer
elements.optional_dependency: dolfinx -- from the hash-pinned conda-forge lock integrations/fenicsx/environment.lock, created by tools/fenicsx_env.py; deliberately not a wheel dependency
elements.boundary: a verifier, never a producer: it admits or refuses a slab result and nothing it computes is admitted as a result. One problem class, the transient slab. Run single-process with MPI offered only self and shared-memory transports (D-2026-124). Executed on a hosted runner with the runtime REQUIRED (the harness-integrations fenicsx and end-to-end jobs).
elements.verification: python tools/fenicsx_acceptance.py --out fenicsx_acceptance.json  # with HARNESS_FENICSX_PYTHON set; the hosted fenicsx and end-to-end jobs
open_items: one problem class only: no FEniCSx check exists for the two-node RC network or the Langmuir capture model

elements.name: FMI 3.0 co-simulation (FMU runtime and boundary)
elements.authority: an FMU result is a SIMULATION_RESULT, NON_AUTHORITATIVE, admitted only through the independent check scientific/checks/fmu_rc2.py and a distinct reviewer
elements.optional_dependency: fmpy -- from the hash-pinned integrations/fmi/runtime.lock, in its own runtime (tools/isolated_runtime.py)
elements.boundary: one generic FMU (integrations/fmi/thermal_rc2, a two-node thermal RC network) is built from C against hash-checked FMI 3.0 headers, loaded by fmpy, stepped, its state serialized, restored and replayed; P2-P5 hold for it; its fault twin is REJECTED by the independent check. Executed on a hosted runner (the harness-integrations fmi and end-to-end jobs). Its bytes are claimed identical between two builds on one host only.
elements.verification: python tools/fmi_acceptance.py  # with HARNESS_FMI_PYTHON set; the hosted fmi and end-to-end jobs

elements.name: Governed authority substrate
elements.authority: agent_substrate: the authenticated event log and the authority store's gate decide admission; agent_substrate/reconstruct.py is the independent second reader
elements.boundary: decides admission of results and computes none: no scientific module imports it (tests/test_agent_substrate_isolation.py), and nothing learned or proposed reaches VERIFIED except through a governed run, an independent check and a distinct reviewer
elements.verification: python -m pytest tests/test_agent_*.py  # and the agent-substrate workflow's mutation shards

elements.name: Generic scientific layer
elements.authority: scientific: models produce ResultBundles, checks return VerificationResults, the authority store admits
elements.boundary: imports nothing of the agent substrate and nothing the repository retired (tests/test_agent_substrate_isolation.py, tools/repo_content_audit.py); an HDF5 bundle is a representation, never evidence of admission

elements.name: AI proposal ingress
elements.authority: agent_substrate/authority.py: a proposal is NON_AUTHORITATIVE data; only a governed run, an independent check and a distinct reviewer reach a decision
elements.boundary: recorded-fixture and external-client adapters behind one envelope; no provider SDK and no network in the trusted core; a proposal is never authority, whoever or whatever made it

retired.why: both candidate kernels were REJECTED by measurement (no production call site; parity dependent on the host's SIMD dispatch; a 0.61x workload speed), and the kernels served only the retired hardware programme's solver, removed with it. No Rust scientific backend exists.
